Worthless. Ends with a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ series of QTEs. Because that's the pinacle of combat mechanics here. That's what they saved for the very end. If they're so damn great, why isn't the rest of the game like that? Why save that turd for the finale? Surely a turd that magnificent should be spread through out the game, advertised as the most brilliant combat mechanic they apparently believe it is.

If you get past the crashing that is. 

Oh and Multiplayer is deader than the Emperor.

Story is the one space marine story they've set on repeat for the past 40k years.

This is a fantastic game that is well worth the money (during one of Relic's annual sales). A must-have for any Warhammer 40k fan, as it continues Relic's tradition of trying to be as accurate as possible to the feel and spirit of the 40k universe.

The gameplay is a good balance between third-person shooting and melee combat. It is challenging while still making you feel like the superhuman killing machine you are. It has a good variety of weapons, including bolters, plasma guns, lascannons, and melta weapons for ranged, and chainswords, power axes, and even thunderhammers for melee. My favorite combo is a jump pack with a thunderhammer, which allows you to smash the God-Emperor's enemies with the necessary amount of righteous fury.

The music and sound design was surprisingly good, with very good sound quality and an appropriately epic tone. It has some fantastic setpieces for the levels, like giant cathedrals and bridges decked out by the Adeptus Mechanicus. In general, it has very high production values and stays true to the lore.

It had me truly awestruck at times, as I am a huge fan of the 40k universe and have read tons of the books, but even people new to the franchise should appreciate the grand scale of it all.

Get it as soon as it goes on sale.
